name: Planning
one_liner: Agile plans more than traditional projects — just continuously and at three granularities.
purpose: The common misperception that agile does not plan comes from the value 'Responding to change over following a plan' — which refers to following a plan, not to planning. The amount of planning effort in agile is greater than in traditionally managed projects, and its intensity is spread throughout the whole project lifecycle. PM²-Agile proposes sufficient upfront planning and documentation to comply with IT governance and project management requirements, which then guides iterative and incremental planning.
meta: The value rejects following a plan, not planning
Do the planning, throw away the Plan

items: 'Responding to change over following a plan' refers to following a plan, not to planning
Agile planning involves more effort than traditionally managed projects
Planning intensity is spread throughout the whole project lifecycle
From maintaining the Work Items List to stand-ups, success depends on effective planning
Detail, granularity and format of the plans
The key players involved in the planning activities
Measures — iterations, story points and velocity instead of person-hours
Releases based on a cut-off date rather than well-defined requirements
Production founded on increments integrating client and stakeholder feedback
Planning cycles and scope are decided per the cycle they belong to and the nature of the project
Planning is more important than plans: 'Do the planning, throw away the Plan'

fields.what: One of the commonest misperceptions about agile relates to planning and originates from the value on responding to change.
fields.pollux: Gantt hears 'agile' and assumes POLLUX has no schedule.

fields.what: The agile value refers to following a plan; it does not devalue the act of planning itself.
fields.pollux: You show Gantt three plans that exist and are maintained continuously.

fields.what: The amount of planning effort in agile involves more effort in comparison to traditionally managed projects.
fields.pollux: Planning happens every fortnight rather than once before execution.

fields.what: The intensity of planning activities is spread throughout the whole project lifecycle rather than concentrated upfront.
fields.pollux: Release Planning runs at least once per iteration across eighteen months.

fields.what: Maintaining the Work Items List, estimating work item effort, Stand-up meetings and iteration planning all count as planning.
fields.pollux: Curie's list, the team's estimates and the daily stand-up are all planning.

fields.what: Agile plans differ in detail, granularity and format, and in the various key players involved in planning activities.
fields.pollux: WIL, Release Plan and Iteration Plan give three levels of detail.

fields.what: Planning plays an important role in integrating and coordinating people's efforts across different involvement levels and planning horizons.
fields.pollux: Coordinates the in-house team with two seconded Levallois Systems members.

fields.what: Agreements must be established so certain plan elements, including presentation and granularity, are accessible and transparent to all.
fields.pollux: Gantt and the team agree what a release-level plan must show.

fields.what: Without such agreements it is difficult to commit resources or synchronise various parallel work streams.
fields.pollux: Unagreed formats would leave the reporting analysts unable to plan their quarter.

fields.what: Lack of visibility and coordination results in disconnects and inefficiencies and increases tension and friction across the organisation.
fields.pollux: The old eleven-spreadsheet chain is exactly that failure, in reporting form.

fields.what: Resource requirements and timelines are measured using iterations, story points and velocity rather than detailed timelines and cost estimates.
fields.pollux: The team sizes work in points; the budget stays €4.6 m and 1,850 PD.

fields.what: Releases are based on a cut-off date as opposed to well-defined requirements, and production integrates feedback into increments.
fields.pollux: Release 2 ships on 28 Jun 2029 with what is ready by then.

fields.what: Managing and Directing stakeholders usually prefer complete plans upfront; involving and educating them demonstrates the agile process's efficacy.
fields.pollux: Conflict 1 — Medici asks why he should fund an undefined deliverable.

fields.what: PM²-Agile proposes sufficient upfront planning and documentation complying with IT governance and project management requirements, guiding later iterative planning.
fields.pollux: Development Handbook and Development Work Plan baselined 27 Nov 2028.

fields.what: Cycles decided per cycle and project nature; everybody is involved in planning; planning is more important than plans.
fields.pollux: Every POLLUX role plans something, from Curie's list to Eiffel's estimates.

traps: Agile planning takes more effort than traditional planning, not less.
The agile value rejects following a plan, not the act of planning.
Releases are cut off by date, not by completing well-defined requirements.
PM²-Agile still requires sufficient upfront planning for IT governance compliance.
'Throw away the Plan' targets the artefact, never the planning activity.
